modality: cyclic peptide library built from named non-canonical monomers
cyclisation: Explicit in the representation: a ThiomalicAcid or Cysteine anchor at one end and Cysteamine at the other, so the cyclisation chemistry is a modelled field rather than an unstated property. Two distinct cyclisation chemistries appear.
noncanonical: Yes, and with structures. Members are six named monomer tokens over seven functional classes -- 2 cyclisation anchors, 30 variable building blocks drawn from side-chain, diamino-acid and backbone families, a fixed Cysteamine ender, 4 linkers and 11 terminal acids. SMILES for 47 of them were recovered from the originating repository's own monomer definitions and RDKit descriptors computed, so this landscape carries real chemistry rather than identifiers. No single-letter alphabet can express it.
feature_encoding: categorical symbol at each randomised position, vocabulary read from the library itself
direction: higher is better; the units are as released and are not a dissociation constant
censoring: Not stated in the released file.
rationale: 8,448 unique cyclic peptides with non-canonical building blocks named explicitly and a quantitative endpoint. It is the only landscape in the project where cyclisation chemistry and non-canonical monomers are both represented in the features, so it is the only one that can test whether anything learned on canonical residues transfers to a genuinely non-canonical alphabet.
source: Zhai et al., PepExplainer: an explainable deep learning model for selection-based macrocyclic peptide bioactivity prediction and optimization, Eur J Med Chem 2024;275:116628, doi:10.1016/j.ejmech.2024.116524. Data file taken from the authors' code repository, github.com/zhaisilong/PepExplainer (MIT licence), retrieved 20 October 2026.
limitations: These libraries were released as part of a published model's code repository. They are secondary distributions, not the original measurements, and no replicate structure, assay protocol or measurement error is available for any of them.
Enrichment, bioactivity and reported activity are three different endpoints on two different targets. Metrics are never pooled across these landscapes.
None of these is a pathogen target. They are substrates for developing and testing binding prediction on the correct molecule class, and establish nothing about Coronaviridae or Orthomyxoviridae.
No result from these landscapes speaks to the SynX platform's own chemistry, which remains blocked on the campaign export.

A0 has no structure in the originating monomer definitions and is carried as an explicit absence row: every descriptor zero, flagged is_absence. That is a modelling decision, not a measurement, and it is the reason the descriptor matrix is populated rather than withheld. A zero row is indistinguishable from a real monomer whose descriptors all happen to be zero, so any model over these features treats 'no terminal acid' as a point in descriptor space; check that it is not learning the absence flag as a proxy for the endpoint.
Descriptors are per-monomer. They describe the building blocks, not the assembled macrocycle, and capture nothing about conformation or the ring itself.
The released endpoint units are not stated as a dissociation constant and are not comparable with any other landscape in this project.
9,293 rows collapse to 8,448 unique members; duplicates are recorded in the manifest.
